analysis.evidence: וּבְנֵי כוּשׁ means “and the sons of Cush.” The five names that follow identify Cush as their father.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun without a prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: סְבָא is the first name listed after וּבְנֵי כוּשׁ, “and the sons of Cush.” The later שְׁבָא, Sheba, is listed among the sons of Raamah.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun with no prefix or suffix.

evidence.note: The heading וּבְנֵי כוּשׁ identifies Havilah as a son of Cush.

article.name: חֲוִילָה
article.summary: Genesis 10:7 names Havilah among the sons of Cush. The derivation of the name is uncertain.

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for חֲוִילָה. The existing geographical article covers the land named in Genesis 2:11.
draft.definition: Havilah, a personal name borne by a son of Cush.
draft.evidence: Genesis 10:7 lists Havilah between Seba and Sabtah among the sons of Cush.

analysis.evidence: וּבְנֵי כוּשׁ introduces the sons of Cush. The conjunction joins Havilah to Seba in that list. The verse gives no etymology for the name.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וַ takes pataḥ before the initial ḥaṭef-pataḥ of the proper noun חֲוִילָה.

evidence.note: Under וּבְנֵי כוּשׁ, “and the sons of Cush,” סַבְתָּה appears between Havilah and Raamah.

article.name: סַבְתָּה
article.summary: Genesis names Sabtah among the sons of Cush. The meaning of his name is uncertain.

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for Sabtah. Leave the root unassigned because the verse supplies no evidence connecting the name to סבל.
draft.definition: Sabtah, one of the sons of Cush.
draft.evidence: Genesis 10:7 lists סַבְתָּה under בְנֵי כוּשׁ.

analysis.evidence: The heading וּבְנֵי כוּשׁ introduces the sons of Cush. Sabtah is the third name, between Havilah and Raamah. The verse identifies the bearer but gives no derivation for his name.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וְ joins the personal name סַבְתָּה to the preceding name in the list.

analysis.evidence: וּבְנֵי כוּשׁ introduces the sons of Cush and places Raamah between Sabtah and Sabteca. The later phrase וּבְנֵי רַעְמָה names Raamah as the father of Sheba and Dedan.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וְ joins the proper noun רַעְמָה to the preceding name in the list.

evidence.note: Sabteca is the last name in the list of Cush’s sons, immediately before the list of Raamah’s sons.

article.name: סַבְתְּכָא
article.summary: Genesis names Sabteca among the sons of Cush. The meaning of his name is uncertain.

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for Sabteca. The verse gives no support for the supplied root סבל or the gloss “feel a loathing.”
draft.definition: Sabteca is the fifth son named in the list of Cush’s sons in Genesis 10:7.
draft.evidence: Genesis 10:7 places סַבְתְּכָא under בְנֵי כוּשׁ, “sons of Cush.”

analysis.evidence: וּבְנֵי כוּשׁ introduces the sons of Cush. Sabteca follows Raamah and closes that list before וּבְנֵי רַעְמָה introduces Raamah’s sons. The verse identifies the bearer but gives no etymology for his name.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וְ means “and” and introduces the personal name סַבְתְּכָא as the final member of the list.

analysis.evidence: The verse first lists Raamah among the sons of Cush, then repeats his name in וּבְנֵי רַעְמָה, “and the sons of Raamah,” introducing Sheba and Dedan as his sons.
analysis.morphology: Proper noun with no prefix or suffix. It follows the construct plural בְנֵי and names the father.

analysis.evidence: וּבְנֵי רַעְמָה introduces the sons of Raamah and lists שְׁבָא alongside Dedan. The genealogy presents Sheba as the ancestor who gives the people its name. The initial שׁ distinguishes Sheba from סְבָא (Seba) earlier in the verse.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Sheba, the people named for Raamah’s son

evidence.note: The list of Raamah’s sons reads שְׁבָא וּדְדָן, “Sheba and Dedan.”

article.name: דְּדָן
article.summary: Genesis 10:7 names Dedan and Sheba as sons of Raamah. The meaning of Dedan’s name is uncertain.

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for דְּדָן with its etymology unassigned.
draft.definition: Dedan, named alongside Sheba as a son of Raamah.
draft.evidence: Genesis 10:7 lists Dedan second among the sons of Raamah.

analysis.evidence: The phrase וּבְנֵי רַעְמָה, “and the sons of Raamah,” introduces the two names שְׁבָא וּדְדָן, “Sheba and Dedan.” The genealogy identifies Dedan’s father but gives no derivation for the name.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וּ joins the personal name דְּדָן to the preceding name שְׁבָא. The initial ד loses its dagesh after the vowel of the prefix.
